title: Third Work and Holiday visa  (Work and Holiday visa (subclass 462) )

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This visa lets people 18 to 30 years old (inclusive) who currently hold, or who have held, a second Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visa, have a third working holiday in Australia.

sections.heading: Overview > You must
sections.text:
- have previously held 2 subclass 462 visas in Australia. If you haven’t, see the first Work and Holiday visa or second Work and Holiday visa
- if in Australia, hold a substantive visa or your last substantive visa expired less than 28 days ago
- have a passport from an eligible country
- be 18 to 30 years old (inclusive)
- have undertaken 6 months of specified subclass 462 work
- not be accompanied by dependent children
- apply on your own. You can’t include family members in your application.

Help with your visa

If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Overview > With this visa you can
sections.text:
- do short- term work in Australia to help pay for your holiday
- study for up to 4 months
- travel to and from Australia as many times as you want

sections.heading: Overview > Cost
sections.text:
Cost concession

From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Papua New Guinea passport holders who lodge a valid third Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visa application. See About this visa.

To work out what your visa will cost, use the Visa Pricing Estimator. The estimator does not take into account the other costs.

sections.heading: Overview > Processing time
sections.text:
For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

To manage high demand and support the long-term sustainability of the WHM program, we are normalising processing timeframes for most WHM visa applications. The average processing time is expected to be around three months. Do not book flights or make travel, work or study commitments until your visa has been granted.

sections.heading: About this visa > With this visa, you can
sections.text:
- do short- term work in Australia to help pay for your holiday
- study for up to 4 months
- travel to and from Australia as many times as you want

Work

You can do any kind of work on this visa.

Usually, you can only work for the same employer for 6 months.

If the main purpose of your stay is to work, consider a work visa.

Study

You can study for up to 4 months (17 weeks).

If the main purpose of your stay is to study, consider a Student visa.

sections.heading: About this visa > How long you can stay
sections.text:
This depends on your circumstances when we grant the Work and Holiday visa. Your grant notification will tell you how long you can stay in Australia. You can check your visa details and conditions using VEVO.

You are in Australia on your second Work and Holiday visa or a bridging visa

The bridging visa must be the one you were granted after your second Work and Holiday visa expired.

You can stay in Australia for up to 12 months from the date your second Work and Holiday visa expired or would have expired.

You are in Australia on a different visa

You can stay in Australia for 12 months from the date we grant the Work and Holiday visa.

If you are in Australia on an Australian Government endorsed events (COVID-19 Pandemic event) subclass 408 visa, you can stay on your third Work and Holiday visa for up to 12 months from when your Pandemic Event visa expired or would have expired.

Time spent outside Australia after your third Work and Holiday visa starts does not extend the visa period of stay in Australia.

You are outside Australia

You can stay in Australia for 12 months from the date you enter Australia.

You must enter Australia within 12 months of the date we grant the visa. We cannot extend or defer this timeframe.

If you have dual citizenship and hold more than one passport, you must enter Australia on the passport linked to your Work and Holiday visa grant.

You must only apply for a Work and Holiday visa once you are ready to enter Australia on that visa.

Once we grant your Work and Holiday visa and you travel to Australia and are immigration cleared at the border, the 12-month visa period of stay will automatically start upon entry, regardless of the purpose of your visit.

sections.heading: About this visa > Stay longer
sections.text:
You cannot stay in Australia longer by extending this visa. If you want to stay in Australia longer, apply for another visa.

You cannot get a fourth Work and Holiday visa if you have already held three Work and Holiday visas in Australia

To stay longer in Australia, explore your visa options.

Stay longer on a visitor visa

Generally, we don't grant a Visitor visa after you have been in Australia on a Work and Holiday visa.

If you want to apply for a Visitor visa to stay longer in Australia and the Visitor visa would result in you staying longer than 12 consecutive months in Australia, you must show there are exceptional circumstances.

For this visa, exceptional circumstances might be that a close family member in Australia has died or is seriously ill, and you are required to stay in Australia to provide assistance or support.

sections.heading: About this visa > Include family
sections.text:
You cannot include family members in your application.

You cannot be accompanied by dependent children while you are in Australia on this visa.

sections.heading: About this visa > Cost
sections.text:
(concessions apply in limited circumstances)

Cost for eligible Work and Holiday Maker Visa applicants from Papua New Guinea

From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Papua New Guinea passport holders who lodge a valid third Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visa application.

We will charge eligible applicants the lower visa application cost during the application process in ImmiAccount. We will recognise eligible applicants by the valid passport from the specified countries used in the application when they apply.

You might also have to pay for health checks, police certificates and biometrics.

sections.heading: About this visa > Apply from
sections.text:
You can be in or outside Australia when you apply for the visa. You must select your current location at the time you apply.

If you apply when you are in Australia, you must be in Australia when we grant your visa.

If you apply when you are outside Australia, you must be outside Australia when we grant your visa.

If you change location after you apply

You must declare your current location correctly on your Work and Holiday visa application form.

We can only grant you an associated bridging visa if you were in Australia when you applied for your Work and Holiday visa.

We cannot grant you a bridging visa associated to your Work and Holiday visa application if you apply outside Australia then enter Australia on another visa before we decide your application.

If you select the wrong location you will need to amend the information on your application. This may delay processing of your application.

sections.heading: About this visa > Processing times
sections.text:
For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

Your application might take longer to process if:

- you do not fill it in correctly
- you do not include all the documents we need, or we need more information from you
- it takes us time to verify your information

sections.heading: About this visa > Your obligations
sections.text:
You must meet all visa conditions and obey Australian laws.

See the conditions for this visa.

Tax

When you work in Australia on this visa you must pay taxes.

Superannuation

Australia has compulsory superannuation - a retirement savings scheme. Your employer must pay superannuation into your superannuation fund if you earn over a certain amount.

When you leave Australia, you can access your superannuation.

Learn more about compulsory superannuation.

sections.heading: About this visa > Health insurance
sections.text:
We strongly recommend you take out health insurance to cover any unforeseen medical treatment you might need in Australia. You are personally liable for all your healthcare costs while you are in Australia. Insurance can help limit your financial liability.

See what we consider adequate health insurance.

Learn more about health insurance for overseas visitors.

Reciprocal healthcare agreements

Some countries have a reciprocal healthcare agreement with Australia. Find out more from Services Australia about reciprocal healthcare agreements.

sections.heading: About this visa > Travel
sections.text:
You can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want while the visa is in effect.

The time you spend outside Australia after your visa commences does not extend the visa period of stay in Australia.

sections.heading: About this visa > Visa record
sections.text: We will digitally link your visa to your passport. You will not get a label in your passport.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have this passport
sections.text:
You must be a citizen of and hold a valid passport from one of these countries:

- Argentina
- Austria
- Brazil
- Chile
- China, People's Republic of
- Czech Republic
- Ecuador
- Greece
- Hungary
- India
- Indonesia
- Israel
- Luxembourg
- Malaysia
- Mongolia
- Papua New Guinea (PNG)
- Peru
- Poland
- Portugal
- San Marino
- Singapore
- Slovak Republic
- Slovenia
- Spain
- Switzerland (from 1 Jan 2022)
- Thailand
- Türkiye
- Uruguay
- USA
- Vietnam

sections.heading: Eligibility > Current or previous visa
sections.text:
You must:

- hold or have previously held a second Work and Holiday visa (subclass 462) in Australia or a bridging visa that came into effect when your second Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visa expired
- if in Australia, hold a substantive visa or your last substantive visa expired less than 28 days ago
- have complied with all the conditions on your previous Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visas

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have enough money
sections.text:
You must have enough money to:

- support yourself while you are in Australia
- leave Australia at the end of your stay

This is usually about AUD5,000 for your initial stay, plus the fare to where you are going after leaving Australia.

If you are applying in Australia, you don’t need to provide evidence. If you are applying outside Australia and don’t attach evidence to your application, processing may be delayed if we need to contact you to request further information.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Specified subclass 462 work
sections.text: You must have completed 6 months of specified subclass 462 work.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be this age
sections.text:
You must be 18 to 30 years old (inclusive) when you apply.

** You must apply for your visa before you turn 31 years old in Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST)/Australian Eastern Daylight Savings Time (AEDST). The deadline to lodge an application is midnight AEST/AEDST the day before your 31st birthday. This time applies even if you are applying from outside Australia.

Note that AEST/AEDST will be different to when your birthday ends in your country due to time differences between countries.

*** Avoid submitting your application on your birthday, if possible.

We can still grant you the visa if you apply for it at 30 but turn 31 years old before we make a decision. You must still meet all other requirements.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet the character requirement
sections.text: You must meet our character requirement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Pay your debts to the Australian Government
sections.text: If you or any family members (including those who don't apply for the visa with you) owe the Australian government money, you or they must have paid it back or arranged to pay it back.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Not had a visa cancelled or an application refused
sections.text:
We will consider your immigration history when we make a decision on your application, which means you might not be eligible for this visa if you have had a visa cancelled or refused.

In some circumstances you may still apply for a permanent visa if you have had a visa cancelled or an application refused see Limitations on applications in Australia.

If applying for a visa from outside Australia see Can I go to Australia.

If you want immigration assistance, see Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text: You must meet all of the following eligibility criteria to be eligible for this visa.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Organise health exams
sections.text:
You might need to have health examinations. You can complete them before you apply or you can wait and have them if we tell you to.

Find out the examinations you need and how to arrange them if you want to have them before you apply.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Get help with your application
sections.text:
Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be:

- a registered migration agent
- a legal practitioner, or
- an exempt person.

You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa matter.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Identity documents
sections.text:
Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates.

Also provide a copy of your birth certificate showing both your parents’ names. If you don’t have a birth certificate and you can’t get one, provide a copy of the identification pages of one of these:

- a family book showing both your parents’ names
- government-issued identification
- a court-issued document that verifies your identity

If you have changed your name, provide proof such as:

- a marriage or divorce certificate
- change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority
- documents that show other names you have been known by

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Enough money for your stay and to leave
sections.text:
Provide evidence you have enough money for your stay in Australia. This is usually AUD5,000.

You must also show us you have enough money to buy a ticket to leave Australia at the end of your stay, or that you already have the ticket.

If you are applying in Australia, you don’t need to provide evidence. If you are applying outside Australia and don’t attach evidence to your application, processing may be delayed if we need to contact you to request further information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Proof of specified subclass 462 work
sections.text:
Provide proof that you have completed 6 months of specified subclass 462 work on your previous WHM visa (or in other eligible circumstances). The proof must cover all periods you worked.

You can include any of the following:

- pay slips or other evidence of payment such as Australian bank statements

- piece rate agreement with your employer, if you were paid piece rates. The agreement must show the pay rate per piece and how it is measured
- group certificates
- payment summaries
- tax returns
- employer references
- a written and signed agreement setting out any lawful deductions in pay

We might contact your employer(s) to check your work claims.

If you have completed volunteer bushfire or flood recovery work, provide:

- a signed letter from your volunteer coordinator or host including:

- your personal details including passport number
- description of volunteer duties undertaken
- location of volunteer work including postcode(s)
- number of days you provided volunteer assistance

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Character documents
sections.text:
We might ask you to provide:

- an Australian police certificate if you have spent a total of 12 months or more in Australia in the last 10 years since you turned 16. We only accept complete disclosure National Police Certificates issued by the Australian Federal Police. We do notaccept standard disclosure certificates or national police certificates issued by Australian state or territory police
- an overseas police certificate from every country, including your home country, where you spent a total of 12 months or more in the last 10 years since you turned 16
- military service records or discharge papers if you served in the armed forces of any country

We will let you know if you need to give us these documents.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Tell us you are getting help
sections.text:
To nominate someone to:

- receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount if you applied online, or send with your paper application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Translate
sections.text:
Have all non-English documents translated into English.

Provide original and translated documents in your application.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating

These details must be in English.

Note: You do not need to have any documents certified.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Scan or photograph
sections.text:
Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour.

The scans and photos must be clear.

If a document is more than one page, save it all as one file.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Attach
sections.text:
Attach a document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing.

Learn more about attaching documents.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Provide accurate information
sections.text: Provide accurate information. See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide true information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Apply online
sections.text:
- Log in or create an ImmiAccount.
- Attach documents.
- Pay the application fee. We will not process your application until you pay the fee.
- Note the transaction reference number.

Applicants with dependent children

You can’t apply online if you are the parent of a child under the age of 18.

Work and Holiday visa holders cannot be accompanied by dependent children at any time during their stay in Australia. While it is possible to obtain a Work and Holiday visa if you have a child, your child cannot join you in Australia at any time while you are on your Work and Holiday visa – not even for one day.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply
sections.text:
See what you can and must do after you apply.

We will let you know when we have received your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Travel > You applied in Australia
sections.text:
Tell us if you want to travel outside Australia while we process your application. We need to know because you must be in Australia when we decide your visa.

If you leave Australia, make sure you have a valid visa to return.

You can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want while the visa is valid.

Time spent outside Australia does not extend the visa.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Travel > You applied outside Australia
sections.text: Do not arrange to travel to Australia until we let you know, in writing, that we have granted you the visa.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Biometrics
sections.text: We might ask for biometrics. We will let you know if you need to provide them.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Health exams
sections.text: If you didn't have health examinations before you applied, we will let you know if you need them.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Attach more information
sections.text:
If you didn't attach all documents when you applied, attach them as soon as you can in ImmiAccount .

We might also ask you to provide more information.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Mistakes on your application
sections.text:
Let us know as soon as you can if you made a mistake on your application.

Complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers and attach it in ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Help with your application
sections.text:
Let us know if you no longer want someone to:

- receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount if you applied online, or send to the office where you submitted your application.

For more information, see Who can help you with your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Tell us if things change after you submit your application but before we decide your visa.

Things you need to let us know about include:

- you want to withdraw your application
- changes to your passport
- changes to your relationship status
- the birth of a child

sections.heading: Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
We will let you know our decision in writing.

If we grant your visa, we will tell you:

- your visa grant number
- the date your visa starts
- your visa conditions

Keep a copy of the decision notification with you when in Australia.

If we refuse your visa, we will tell you:

- why we refused the visa
- if you have a right to a review of the decision

Step Summary

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Outside Australia
sections.text:
Before you travel

You must only apply for a third Work and Holiday visa once you are ready to enter Australia on that visa. Once we grant your Work and Holiday visa, you can use the visa to enter Australia.

After we grant your third Work and Holiday visa you do not need to apply for another visa, such as an eVisitor (subclass 651), a Transit (subclass 771), or an Electronic Travel Authority (ETA) (subclass 601) visa to enter Australia.

If we grant you an eVisitor or Transit visa after your Work and Holiday visa

If we grant you another visa (such as an eVisitor or Transit visa) after the grant of your third Work and Holiday visa, your Work and Holiday visa (and related work rights) will cease as soon as we grant that other visa.

If your third Work and Holiday visa ceased due to the grant of another visa, such as an eVisitor or Transit visa, and you entered Australia on that other visa, you may be able to apply for another third Work and Holiday visa while you are in Australia. You will need to pay the Visa Application Charge (VAC) if you apply again.

If we grant you an Electronic Travel Authority (ETA) (subclass 601) visa

If you enter Australia after the grant of your Work and Holiday visa, the 12-month period of stay on your visa will automatically start on that day.

The Work and Holiday visa period will start regardless of the purpose of your visit, even if:

- you just want to transit through Australia on your way to another country

or

- we have granted you an Electronic Travel Authority (ETA) (subclass 601) visa.

An ETA grant will not cease your Work and Holiday visa

An ETA cannot be in effect at the same time as your Work and Holiday visa. When you enter Australia your Work and Holiday visa will commence. Your ETA will come into effect after the Work and Holiday visa ceases.

Check your travel documents are up to date

Your Work and Holiday visa will be linked to the passport you declared on your application. If you obtain a new passport after your visa is granted, you must tell us your new passport details. See how to tell us if your situation changes.

If you do not update your passport details, you will face delays at your overseas departure point and may not be permitted to board your flight.

You must:

- have a Work and Holiday visa that is in effect to enter Australia. You do not need a separate visa to enter Australia. We recommend that you keep a copy of your grant letter (electronic or paper) while travelling
- hold a valid passport issued by a Work and Holiday participant country
- enter Australia using the passport linked to your WHM visa grant. This applies even if you have dual citizenship and hold more than one valid passport.

At the border

Completing an Incoming Passenger Card

All people arriving in Australia must complete the Incoming Passenger Card. You will be given this card on board.

Leaving the airport faster

We have an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport, if you have one. You may be able to leave the airport faster if you use SmartGate.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > In Australia
sections.text:
With this visa you can:

- have a holiday
- do any kind of work
- study for up to 4 months
- travel to and from Australia as many times as you want

Work

Usually, you can only work for the same employer for 6 months.

You can work another 6 months with an employer you worked for on your first and/or second visa.

To see your conditions for work, use VEVO.

You must pay taxes when you work.

You are protected by Australian workplace law. See information for migrant workers and your workplace rights and entitlements.

Superannuation

If you earn over a certain amount, your employer must pay superannuation into your superannuation fund. Australia has compulsory superannuation- a retirement savings scheme.

When you leave Australia, you can access your superannuation.

Study

You can study for up to 4 months (17 weeks).

To see your study entitlements use VEVO.

Travel

You can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want while the visa is in effect.

Time spent outside Australia after your visa commences does not extend the visa period of stay in Australia.

How long you can stay

This depends on your circumstances when you applied and when we grant the visa. Your grant notification will tell you how long you can stay in Australia and you can also use VEVO to check your visa details and conditions.

You were in Australia on your second subclass 462 visa or a bridging visa

The bridging visa must be the one you were granted after your second Work and Holiday visa expired.

You can stay in Australia for up to 12 months from the date your second Work and Holiday visa expired or would have expired.

You were in Australia on a different visa

You can stay for 12 months from the date we grant the visa.

If you were in Australia on an Australian Government endorsed events (COVID-19 Pandemic event) subclass 408 visa, you can stay on your third Work and Holiday visa for up to 12 months from when your Pandemic Event visa expired or would have expired.

You were outside Australia

You can stay for 12 months from the date you enter Australia on the visa.

You must enter Australia within 12 months of the date we grant the visa. We cannot extend or defer this timeframe.

To see when you must leave, use VEVO.

Time spent outside Australia after the visa starts does not extend the visa.

Stay longer

You cannot stay in Australia longer by extending this visa.

You cannot get a fourth Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visa if you have held three Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visas in Australia.

You must apply for a different visa if you want to stay longer.

See your visa options.

What you must do on this visa

You must meet all visa conditions and obey Australian laws.

See your conditions in your visa grant letter or VEVO.

Proving you have a visa

To prove you have a visa and show your conditions to someone, use VEVO.

Tell us if things change

Things you need to let us know about include:

- changes to your passport
- changes to your relationship status
- the birth of a child

See how to tell us if your situation changes.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Leaving Australia
sections.text:
Before you leave

Check your travel documents.

You must have a valid passport or other travel document to leave Australia.

At the border

Departures SmartGate

We have an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You may be able to leave the airport faster if you use SmartGate.

After you leave

Getting your superannuation

You are likely to have some money in a superannuation fund if you worked in Australia and you are:

- aged 18 years or older
- paid $450 or more before tax in a month

See how to access your super.

Proving you have been to Australia

Request your international movement records to get proof of your travel in and out of Australia.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > You must
sections.text: - You need to be holding a subclass 457 visa

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > How long you can stay
sections.text: This is a permanent visa. You can stay in Australia indefinitely

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility

Answer the questions below to see if you meet them, and which requirements that apply to you.
